text.tspan: Primitives copy the value. Objects copy the reference: two names, one object.
let b = a; // copies the number
Two separate boxes. Changing one cannot
touch the other. Same for string, boolean,
const y = x; // copies the arrow, not the box
One object, two names. Arrays and functions
are objects too, so they behave the same way.
To get a real copy, spread it: const z = { ...x } or const arr2 = [ ...arr ]
But spread is SHALLOW: a nested object is still shared. Use structuredClone(x) for a deep copy.
Also why const does not mean immutable: it fixes the arrow, not the box it points at.
